claims.explanation: Nocodazole kills cells by disrupting microtubule polymerization, and the selective pattern is best explained by mitotic/checkpoint and microtubule-regulatory context rather than by any single lineage. TP53 loss is common in both sensitive and resistant lines, so it is not sufficient; instead, sensitivity tracks with features that increase reliance on microtubule-dependent mitosis or reduce drug efflux/checkpoint adaptation, while resistance associates with EGFR/MAPK activation and other protective programs. The virtual-cell response (AURKA up, CDK1/TOP2A/UBE2C down) supports a mitotic-spindle mechanism.

features.basis: TP53 mutation is highly enriched among selectively killed lines, consistent with impaired checkpoint/apoptosis adaptation after spindle damage
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines are overrepresented among least-affected lines, suggesting EGFR/MAPK signaling protects against nocodazole
BRAF-mutant melanoma and other BRAF-mutant lines appear among sensitive lines, possibly reflecting MAPK-driven mitotic dependency
AURKA is upregulated in the virtual-cell response and Aurora kinases regulate mitotic spindle assembly/checkpoint, a known nocodazole-relevant pathway
CDK1 is downregulated in the virtual-cell response and is the core mitotic kinase whose activity determines sensitivity to spindle poisons
TOP2A is downregulated in the virtual-cell response and topoisomerase II is required for mitotic chromosome separation, linking to nocodazole-sensitive mitosis
UBE2C is downregulated in the virtual-cell response and controls mitotic progression/checkpoint, a pathway engaged by nocodazole
PTEN mutation appears in several sensitive lines (endometrial, breast, glioma), possibly via PI3K/AKT-mediated mitotic vulnerability
NF1 mutation appears in multiple sensitive lines, consistent with RAS/MAPK pathway activation altering mitotic drug response
ARID1A mutation is recurrent among sensitive lines, suggesting chromatin-remodeling loss may increase mitotic stress sensitivity
KMT2D mutation is recurrent among sensitive lines, possibly reflecting epigenetic modulation of mitotic gene programs
KRAS mutation is enriched among least-affected lines, suggesting oncogenic RAS/MAPK signaling reduces nocodazole sensitivity
